newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: IMF stops $185 mln stand-by loan to Uzbekistan.
newsitem.headline: IMF stops $185 mln stand-by loan to Uzbekistan.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund said on Thursday it had suspended disbursements of a $185 million stand-by loan to Uzbekistan because the former Soviet republic had failed to meet the fund's inflation targets.

"Disbursements under the IMF stand-by arrangement have been postponed because of these developments," Mark O'Brien, the IMF's resident representative in Uzbekistan, told a news conference in the Uzbek capital Tashkent. The largely desert nation had already received $92 million of the loan, agreed by the IMF in December 1995.
O'Brien said Uzbekistan's target for 1996 annual inflation was set at around 25 percent but that the actual rate was likely to be in excess of 40 percent. He gave no exact figures.

"Uzbekistan's external trade account in 1996 was hit by lower international prices for cotton exports and a poorer than expected grain harvest," O'Brien explained, saying the Uzbek government had responded by increasing credits to agriculture and limiting access to foreign exchange.

The resulting spread between Uzbekistan's official and black market rates has widened in recent weeks, with the official rate of 55 sums to the dollar way below the black market rate of 105 sums to the dollar on Thursday.

"Inflationary pressures increased and the exchange rates in the (interbank) auction, exchange bureaux and the kerb market diverged," said O'Brien. He added that an IMF mission would visit Tashkent to reassess the situation in January 1997.
